skills.title: Researching Habitats and Rocks
skills.description: Put the steps of a research in order. Pick a good question about habitats, light, or rocks and the best place to find the answer.

skills.title: Fair Tests With Light and Sound
skills.description: Pick the fair test that changes only one thing, like testing how sound travels through different materials. Put the steps of an experiment in order.

skills.title: Design, Build, Test Machines
skills.description: Put the steps for designing and building a device in order. Pick what to change to make it work better.

skills.title: Safe Science Investigating
skills.description: Pick the safe way to use tools, lights, and materials. Choose the right gear to wear, like goggles or gloves.

skills.title: Sharing Findings With an Audience
skills.description: Pick the best way to share what you found for different people and reasons. Match science words to what they mean.

skills.title: Code That Makes Output
skills.description: Look at a few lines of code and pick what output they make, like a sound, a picture, or a message. Pick the code that gives the output you want.

skills.title: Coding, New Tech, and Trades
skills.description: Pick how coding and new technology change daily life and jobs, including skilled trades.

skills.title: Science in Jobs and Subjects
skills.description: Match jobs, including skilled trades, to the science they use to fix real problems. Pick how science works with other subjects to help.

skills.title: Science Ideas From Communities
skills.description: Match science and technology ideas to the communities that gave them to us. Pick how those ideas help people.

skills.title: Habitats Give Living Things Needs
skills.description: Pick how a habitat gives plants and animals food, water, shelter, and space. Match a local habitat to the needs it meets.

skills.title: Communities in a Habitat
skills.description: Pick that a community is different species living and interacting in one habitat. Pick what helps or hurts them in a local habitat, like food, weather, or space.

skills.title: Food Chains
skills.description: Put a food chain in order. Sort living things into producers, consumers, and decomposers.

skills.title: Food Webs
skills.description: Pick how many food chains link together to make a food web. Pick what happens in the web when one link changes.

skills.title: Carnivores, Herbivores, Omnivores
skills.description: Sort animals into carnivores, herbivores, and omnivores by what they eat.

skills.title: Adaptations for Habitats
skills.description: Match body parts of plants and animals, like cactus spines or webbed feet, to how they help the living thing survive in its habitat.

skills.title: Habitats Have Limits
skills.description: Pick why a habitat can only support so many plants and animals, like limited food, water, and space.

skills.title: People and Habitats
skills.description: Pick good and bad ways people's actions affect habitats and communities. Think about how different people see it.

skills.title: When a Species Disappears
skills.description: Pick what happens to a habitat and its community when a species becomes scarce or extinct. Pick actions that help prevent it.

skills.title: Natural and Artificial Light
skills.description: Sort light sources into natural ones, like the Sun and fireflies, and artificial ones, like lamps.

skills.title: Makes Light or Reflects Light
skills.description: Sort objects and living things into ones that make their own light and ones that only reflect light, like a star and the Moon.

skills.title: How Light Behaves
skills.description: Pick facts about light: it travels in straight paths, and it can be absorbed, reflected, or refracted.

skills.title: How Sound Behaves
skills.description: Pick facts about sound: it travels as a wave through a medium, and it can be absorbed, reflected, or changed in pitch and loudness.

skills.title: Vibrations Make Sound
skills.description: Pick how a vibrating object makes sound waves, like a guitar string or a drum.

skills.title: Materials, Light, and Sound
skills.description: Sort materials by how they treat light and sound, like see-through, shiny, or sound-blocking.

skills.title: Light With or Without Heat
skills.description: Sort light sources into ones that give off light and heat, like a candle, and ones that give little heat, like an LED.

skills.title: Eyes, Ears, and Devices
skills.description: Label sense organs like the eye and ear. Match devices like glasses, microphones, and telescopes to the light or sound property they use.

skills.title: Light and Sound Devices Help Us
skills.description: Pick how devices that use light or sound, like alarms and lasers, help or cause problems for people.

skills.title: Light and Sound Pollution
skills.description: Pick how light and sound from technology, like bright city lights or loud machines, affect nature and different people.

skills.title: Machines in Daily Life
skills.description: Pick machines we use every day and what each one is for.

skills.title: Parts of a Mechanism
skills.description: Label parts of mechanisms like gears, belts, cranks, and levers. Pick what each part does.

skills.title: Passing Motion Along
skills.description: Pick how gears, belts, and chains pass motion, including turning motion, from one part to another.

skills.title: Changing Motion
skills.description: Pick how mechanisms change motion, like turning round motion into up and down, or making it faster, slower, or a new direction.

skills.title: How Machines Change Forces
skills.description: Pick how machines make a force bigger, smaller, or point a different way, like a lever or a gear set.

skills.title: Machines in People's Lives
skills.description: Pick how machines change daily life for people in different communities.

skills.title: Comparing Machines and Nature
skills.description: Compare machines with the same job, like a gas mower and a push mower. Pick which is better for the environment.

skills.title: The Rock Cycle
skills.description: Put the rock cycle in order. Pick how heat, pressure, and settling make igneous, sedimentary, and metamorphic rocks.

skills.title: Three Kinds of Rock
skills.description: Match looks and features, like layers, crystals, or bands, to igneous, sedimentary, and metamorphic rocks.

skills.title: Sorting Rocks and Minerals
skills.description: Sort rocks and minerals using tests like hardness, colour, streak, and luster.

skills.title: Everyday Uses of Rocks
skills.description: Match rocks and minerals, like granite, salt, and graphite, to how we use them every day.

skills.title: Fossils and Earth's History
skills.description: Put the steps of how a fossil forms in order. Pick what fossils tell us about Earth long ago.

skills.title: First Nations, Métis, Inuit Rock Knowledge
skills.description: Match rocks and minerals to the purposes First Nations, Métis, and Inuit peoples chose them for, like tools, pipes, and carving.

skills.title: Earthquakes, Volcanoes, and People
skills.description: Pick how geological events like volcanoes, earthquakes, and erosion affect people and nature.

skills.title: Mining and Rock Products
skills.description: Pick good and bad effects of digging up, making, recycling, and throwing away rock and mineral products. Think about how different people see it.
